label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
@Deirdre Fortuin thank you for asking me and not just announcing it. It means a lot.

I'll be honest, this one is hard. Noma has been with me in the Seahorses for all three years, since my very first year of teaching. She taught me so much of the job, from the sign-in sheets to surviving the parent WhatsApp group. The kids adore her. Her isiXhosa songs at morning ring are a big part of our room, and they ask for "Noma's song" every single day. In Term 2, when one of my little ones was really struggling, she was the only one who could calm him. She sat with him under the jungle gym for as long as it took.

I do understand the numbers, and I'm not going to fight it. Bronwyn needs the help more, and it helps that Noma will still be just across the courtyard. I just wanted you to know it matters, and that I'd really like us to get the handover right.

The first weeks of Grade R are the hardest, with new kids crying at the gate, and a new assistant on top of that is a lot all at once. So if you're able to put two things to SMT on Friday:

1. Could Charlene come in for a day or two in the last week of term (1-4 Dec) to meet Noma and see our routine? It's much easier to see how the room works than to have it explained.

2. Could Noma pop in for morning ring in the first week back, from 14 Jan, even if it's just 15 minutes? Two of next year's kids already know her from aftercare, so a familiar face would really help them. Charlene only starts on 11 Jan, so it would also help her find her feet before the kids arrive.

Thank you again, Deirdre. I really appreciate how you've handled this.
